newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-NEW ENGLAND CAPTAIN BACKS UNDER-FIRE ROWELL.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-NEW ENGLAND CAPTAIN BACKS UNDER-FIRE ROWELL.

text.p: England captain Phil De Glanville stood firmly behind national coach Jack Rowell on Thursday after bitter comments by Rowell's predecessor Dick Best interrupted preparations for the weekend test against Italy.

Best, elbowed aside when Rowell took over the twin roles of England coach and manager in 1994, predicted his rival would be sacked next year and branded senior Rugby Football Union (RFU) officials as "two-faced and gutless" in a magazine article.
De Glanville, set to lead England for the first time in succession to Will Carling, a long-time ally of Harlequins coach Best, neatly sidestepped the dispute in his debut pre-match press conference.
"As far as the players are concerned it's a non-issue," said De Glanville, who rose to prominence under Rowell's command at Bath.
"We're not bothered by what anybody says outside the squad. People are entitled to their opinions, however right or wrong they may be, but I haven't heard one player talk about it."
Best, still angry at how he was treated by the RFU, claimed in the article Rowell had wasted a year in shaping a new England side by continuing to pick older players such as Dean Richards.
Ironically, Rowell's team to face Italy contains five caps, with Wasps number eight Chris Sheasby replacing the injured Ben Clarke on Thursday, with De Glanville operating a sink-or-swim policy.
"I've said to the new guys we must have them contributing from minute one. There's no honeymoon period for 20-25 minutes for people to get into it.
"It's important everyone kicks off with a good performance. I'll be captain for the first time but I don't feel under any more pressure than anyone else in the team."
